constructs.name: Moral stance-independence / objectivity
constructs.description: Degree to which moral truth or correctness is treated as independent of individual or group attitudes.

constructs.name: Universal applicability of moral claims
constructs.description: Degree to which moral requirements are thought to apply across persons, groups, and contexts.

constructs.name: Moral context-sensitivity
constructs.description: Degree to which morally relevant context can change the correct judgment.

constructs.name: Generalism vs particularism
constructs.description: Whether moral judgment is primarily governed by general principles or irreducibly particular features.

constructs.name: Categorical moral reasons
constructs.description: Degree to which moral reasons bind independently of an agent's contingent goals or preferences.

constructs.name: Moral truth-aptness
constructs.description: Whether moral assertions are treated as the kind of claims that can literally be true or false.

constructs.name: Metaethical family
constructs.description: Derived classification over realist, constructivist, subjectivist, error-theoretic, noncognitivist, and related families.

constructs.name: Moral motivation internalism / externalism
constructs.description: Whether sincere moral judgment is conceptually or necessarily connected to motivation.

constructs.name: Consequence sensitivity
constructs.description: Weight given to aggregate or outcome-based consequences in moral evaluation.

constructs.name: Deontic constraint strength
constructs.description: Strength of moral constraints against otherwise beneficial actions.

constructs.name: Virtue and character orientation
constructs.description: Affinity for evaluating conduct through character, virtues, and practical excellence.

constructs.name: Care and relational orientation
constructs.description: Affinity for relationship-sensitive, dependency-sensitive, and care-centered moral reasoning.

constructs.name: Contractualist non-rejectability
constructs.description: Affinity for principles justifiable to each person under reasonable rejection constraints.

constructs.name: Contractarian mutual advantage
constructs.description: Affinity for morality grounded in mutually advantageous agreement among agents.

constructs.name: Impartial beneficence
constructs.description: Willingness to give equal moral weight to distant or unfamiliar persons and make demanding sacrifices for their welfare.

constructs.name: Instrumental-harm permissiveness
constructs.description: Willingness to cause harm instrumentally when doing so produces sufficiently better outcomes.

constructs.name: Special obligations and partiality
constructs.description: Weight assigned to special obligations to family, friends, associates, or compatriots.

constructs.name: Agent-relative prerogatives / self-priority
constructs.description: Extent to which agents may give their own projects or welfare priority over impersonal demands.

constructs.name: Moral demandingness
constructs.description: Extent to which morality may require substantial sacrifice beyond ordinary expectations.

constructs.name: Doing-allowing asymmetry
constructs.description: Strength of the distinction between causing harm and allowing comparable harm to occur.

constructs.name: Rule-mediated vs direct act evaluation
constructs.description: Whether actions are primarily evaluated through rules/practices or directly by features of the individual act.

constructs.name: Intention and side-effect sensitivity
constructs.description: Importance of intended means versus merely foreseen side effects in moral judgment.

constructs.name: Care
constructs.description: Moral concern with suffering, protection, and care.

constructs.name: Equality
constructs.description: Moral concern with equal treatment and equal standing.

constructs.name: Proportionality
constructs.description: Moral concern with proportional reward, contribution, reciprocity, and desert.

constructs.name: Loyalty
constructs.description: Moral concern with commitment to groups and collective bonds.

constructs.name: Authority
constructs.description: Moral concern with hierarchy, duty, role, and legitimate deference.

constructs.name: Purity
constructs.description: Moral concern with sanctity, degradation, contamination, and purity.

constructs.name: Liberty / opposition to domination
constructs.description: Experimental moral-foundation construct concerning domination, coercion, and liberty.

constructs.name: Self-direction: thought
constructs.description: Importance of freedom to cultivate one's own ideas and abilities.

constructs.name: Self-direction: action
constructs.description: Importance of freedom to determine one's own actions.

constructs.name: Stimulation
constructs.description: Importance of excitement, novelty, and change.

constructs.name: Hedonism
constructs.description: Importance of pleasure and sensuous gratification.

constructs.name: Achievement
constructs.description: Importance of success according to social standards.

constructs.name: Power: dominance
constructs.description: Importance of power through exercising control over people.

constructs.name: Power: resources
constructs.description: Importance of power through control of material and social resources.

constructs.name: Face
constructs.description: Importance of maintaining public image and avoiding humiliation.

constructs.name: Security: personal
constructs.description: Importance of safety in one's immediate environment.

constructs.name: Security: societal
constructs.description: Importance of safety and stability in wider society.

constructs.name: Tradition
constructs.description: Importance of maintaining cultural, family, or religious traditions.

constructs.name: Conformity: rules
constructs.description: Importance of complying with rules, laws, and formal obligations.

constructs.name: Conformity: interpersonal
constructs.description: Importance of avoiding upsetting or harming other people in social interaction.

constructs.name: Humility
constructs.description: Importance of recognizing one's insignificance in the larger scheme.

constructs.name: Benevolence: caring
constructs.description: Importance of devotion to the welfare of close others.

constructs.name: Benevolence: dependability
constructs.description: Importance of being a reliable and trustworthy member of one's in-group.

constructs.name: Universalism: concern
constructs.description: Importance of commitment to equality, justice, and protection of all people.

constructs.name: Universalism: nature
constructs.description: Importance of preservation of the natural environment.

constructs.name: Universalism: tolerance
constructs.description: Importance of acceptance and understanding of people different from oneself.

constructs.name: Theory of well-being
constructs.description: Affinity among experiential/hedonistic, desire-satisfaction, objective-list, and related accounts of well-being.

constructs.name: Aesthetic value objectivity
constructs.description: Whether aesthetic value is objective, response-dependent, conventional, or otherwise constituted.

constructs.name: Fallibilism / revisability
constructs.description: Willingness to treat one's beliefs as revisable in light of new evidence or argument.

constructs.name: Knowledge complexity
constructs.description: Tendency to regard knowledge as complex, interconnected, and developing rather than simple and fixed.

constructs.name: Attainability of truth
constructs.description: Whether human inquiry can sometimes reach objectively correct factual answers while remaining fallible and revisable.

constructs.name: Empirical / sensory evidence reliance
constructs.description: Epistemic weight assigned to observation and sensory evidence.

constructs.name: Rational / a priori reliance
constructs.description: Epistemic weight assigned to reason, conceptual analysis, or a priori justification.

constructs.name: Scientific-method reliance
constructs.description: Epistemic weight assigned to systematic scientific methods.

constructs.name: Testimony and expertise reliance
constructs.description: Epistemic weight assigned to credible testimony and domain expertise.

constructs.name: Tradition as epistemic source
constructs.description: Epistemic weight assigned to inherited tradition and long-standing practice.

constructs.name: Intuition as epistemic source
constructs.description: Epistemic weight assigned to intuition or seeming.

constructs.name: Revelation as epistemic source
constructs.description: Epistemic weight assigned to alleged divine or supernatural revelation.

constructs.name: External-world stance
constructs.description: Direct realism, indirect realism, idealism, skepticism, or related positions regarding the external world.

constructs.name: Theory of justification
constructs.description: Affinity among foundationalist, coherentist, reliabilist, infinitist, and related accounts.

constructs.name: Scientific realism
constructs.description: Degree of commitment to realist interpretation of successful scientific theories and unobservable entities.

constructs.name: Values in science
constructs.description: View of whether and how non-epistemic values may legitimately influence scientific reasoning.

constructs.name: Naturalism / supernatural ontology
constructs.description: Whether reality is exhausted by the natural world or includes irreducibly supernatural entities or powers.

constructs.name: Physicalism / nonphysicalism
constructs.description: Whether everything is fundamentally physical or includes irreducibly nonphysical reality.

constructs.name: Abstract-object realism / nominalism
constructs.description: Whether abstract objects or universals exist independently of concrete particulars and linguistic practices.

constructs.name: Reductionism and emergence
constructs.description: Affinity for reductive versus genuinely emergent explanatory structures.

constructs.name: Teleology / purposiveness in nature
constructs.description: Degree to which natural processes are interpreted as inherently purposive or goal-directed.

constructs.name: Laws of nature: Humean / non-Humean
constructs.description: Competing metaphysical accounts of laws of nature.

constructs.name: Causation model
constructs.description: Competing accounts such as counterfactual, production, regularity, or primitive causal structure.

constructs.name: Metaontology
constructs.description: Whether ontological disputes are substantive, deflationary, quantifier-relative, or otherwise construed.

constructs.name: Temporal ontology
constructs.description: Presentism, eternalism, growing-block, and related positions.

constructs.name: Modal ontology
constructs.description: Commitments concerning possible worlds, modality, and modal realism or actualism.

constructs.name: Consciousness reducibility
constructs.description: Degree to which consciousness is thought reducible to nonconscious physical/functional facts.

constructs.name: Consciousness theory family
constructs.description: Affinity among physicalist identity, functionalist, dualist, panpsychist, eliminativist, and related families.

constructs.name: Personal identity theory
constructs.description: Biological, psychological-continuity, further-fact, reductionist, and related accounts of persistence.

constructs.name: Substantial-self vs process-self orientation
constructs.description: Whether the self is treated as a persisting substance/entity or a constructed/process-like organization.

constructs.name: Extended-mind acceptance
constructs.description: Acceptance that cognitive processes can constitutively extend beyond the biological individual.

constructs.name: Mental-content internalism / externalism
constructs.description: Whether mental content is individuated solely by internal state or partly by external relations.

constructs.name: Identity under transformation
constructs.description: Derived pattern across teleportation, copying, uploading, replacement, and continuity vignettes.

constructs.name: Free-will belief
constructs.description: Whether human beings sometimes act with genuine free will, independently of which compatibility or metaphysical theory explains it.

constructs.name: Determinism belief
constructs.description: Strength of belief that events and choices are determined by prior states and laws/causes.

constructs.name: Moral-responsibility belief
constructs.description: Strength of belief in basic or desert-entailing moral responsibility.

constructs.name: Baseline human benevolence
constructs.description: Belief that humans are naturally capable of or inclined toward benevolence/cooperation.

constructs.name: Baseline human selfishness / competition
constructs.description: Belief that humans are naturally inclined toward selfishness, rivalry, or competition.

constructs.name: Human-nature mutability
constructs.description: Belief that human traits and dispositions are substantially malleable.

constructs.name: Human-nature complexity
constructs.description: Belief that behavior resists simple, single-cause accounts.

constructs.name: Biological causal attribution
constructs.description: Weight assigned to biological and inherited causes of behavior.

constructs.name: Environmental / social causal attribution
constructs.description: Weight assigned to environmental, institutional, and social causes of behavior.

constructs.name: Rational-conscious causal attribution
constructs.description: Weight assigned to conscious reasons and deliberation as causes of behavior.

constructs.name: Unconscious / intrapsychic causal attribution
constructs.description: Weight assigned to unconscious or intrapsychic causes of behavior.

constructs.name: Agency theory family
constructs.description: Derived but explicitly confirmed classification among compatibilist, libertarian, hard-determinist, skeptical, and related positions.

constructs.name: Deity existence
constructs.description: Credence or categorical stance regarding the existence of God or gods.

constructs.name: Personal / agentic deity
constructs.description: Degree to which divinity is understood as personal, intentional, or agentic.

constructs.name: Supernatural reality
constructs.description: Belief in supernatural beings, properties, forces, or realms.

constructs.name: Divine / supernatural intervention
constructs.description: Belief that supernatural agency intervenes in ordinary events.

constructs.name: Miraculous intervention
constructs.description: Belief that events can occur through suspension or extraordinary override of ordinary natural regularities.

constructs.name: Revelatory authority
constructs.description: Authority granted to purported revelation in belief and conduct.

constructs.name: Afterlife / postmortem persistence
constructs.description: Belief that persons or consciousness persist after bodily death.

constructs.name: Cosmic purpose
constructs.description: Belief that the universe or human life has an objective cosmic purpose.

constructs.name: Sacredness orientation
constructs.description: Degree to which entities, places, practices, or values are regarded as sacred or inviolable.

constructs.name: Religious / spiritual centrality
constructs.description: Importance and centrality of religious or spiritual commitments in the person's life.

constructs.name: Divinity model
constructs.description: Theistic, deistic, pantheistic, panentheistic, impersonal-divinity, and related models.

constructs.name: Ontology of life's meaning
constructs.description: Whether meaning is objective, subjectively constructed, plural, absent, or otherwise constituted.

constructs.name: Objective-purpose source
constructs.description: Proposed source of objective meaning or purpose when such meaning is endorsed.

constructs.name: Subjective / constructed meaning
constructs.description: Degree to which agents are thought capable of creating meaningful lives through projects, relations, and commitments.

constructs.name: Existential nihilism
constructs.description: Degree of endorsement that life lacks objective or inherent meaning/value.

constructs.name: World safety
constructs.description: General belief that the world is safe rather than dangerous.

constructs.name: World enticingness / possibility
constructs.description: General belief that the world is interesting, abundant, and full of worthwhile possibilities.

constructs.name: World aliveness / intentional character
constructs.description: General tendency to experience the world as intentional, responsive, or alive.

constructs.name: Optimism vs resignation
constructs.description: General orientation toward possibility of improvement versus resignation or pessimism.

constructs.name: Response to meaninglessness
constructs.description: Derived existential style in response to absence or uncertainty of objective meaning.

constructs.name: Individualism
constructs.description: Priority assigned to persons as independent agents with distinct projects and claims.

constructs.name: Collectivism
constructs.description: Priority assigned to collective identities, goals, and group-level obligations.

constructs.name: Relational / interdependent self
constructs.description: Degree to which identity is understood through constitutive relationships and social roles.

constructs.name: Tolerance of otherness
constructs.description: Acceptance of persons, lifestyles, and groups substantially different from one's own.

constructs.name: Group-dominance preference
constructs.description: Preference for hierarchical dominance of some social groups over others.

constructs.name: Anti-egalitarianism
constructs.description: Opposition to group-based social equality independent of explicit dominance preference.

constructs.name: Cooperation orientation
constructs.description: Belief in and preference for cooperative modes of social interaction.

constructs.name: Competition orientation
constructs.description: Belief in and preference for competitive modes of social interaction.

constructs.name: Scope of moral concern / cosmopolitan concern
constructs.description: Breadth of the circle of persons toward whom substantial moral concern is extended.

constructs.name: Social-category essentialism
constructs.description: Degree to which social categories are treated as deep, natural, fixed, or essence-bearing.

constructs.name: Social-construction orientation
constructs.description: Degree to which social categories and institutions are understood as historically and socially constituted.

constructs.name: Humanity-nature worldview
constructs.description: Higher-order family containing anthropocentrism, ecocentrism, ecological limits, mastery, and harmony/interdependence facets.

constructs.name: Belief in social/world justice
constructs.description: Belief that people generally receive outcomes they deserve or that social reality is fundamentally just.

constructs.name: Legitimacy of coercive political authority
constructs.description: Degree to which states or political institutions can possess a justified right to coerce.

constructs.name: General political obligation
constructs.description: Degree to which persons have a general moral duty to obey political law as such.

constructs.name: Consent requirement for authority
constructs.description: Degree to which legitimate authority requires actual, meaningful, or revocable consent.

constructs.name: Democratic participation / authorization
constructs.description: Weight assigned to democratic participation or authorization in political legitimacy.

constructs.name: Centralization vs decentralization
constructs.description: Preference for concentration versus dispersion of political decision-making authority.

constructs.name: Liberty as noninterference
constructs.description: Importance assigned to freedom from interference.

constructs.name: Freedom as non-domination
constructs.description: Importance assigned to freedom from arbitrary or uncontrolled power.

constructs.name: Positive / capability liberty
constructs.description: Importance assigned to effective capacity or opportunity to pursue valued ends.

constructs.name: Rights as side constraints
constructs.description: Strength of rights-based constraints against pursuit of aggregate or collective goals.

constructs.name: Distributive-principle family
constructs.description: Relative affinities for equality, need, desert, sufficiency, priority, entitlement, and related distributive principles.

constructs.name: Property-right strength
constructs.description: Strength and scope of moral claims attached to private possession, use, transfer, and exclusion.

constructs.name: Collective / common ownership legitimacy
constructs.description: Degree to which common, collective, or social ownership is regarded as legitimate or desirable.

constructs.name: Market coordination preference
constructs.description: Preference for decentralized exchange and price-mediated coordination.

constructs.name: Collective / democratic coordination preference
constructs.description: Preference for collective, participatory, or democratically planned coordination.

constructs.name: Expert / administrative coordination preference
constructs.description: Preference for expert, technocratic, or administrative coordination.

constructs.name: Procedural justice priority
constructs.description: Importance assigned to fair procedures independent of substantive outcomes.

constructs.name: Substantive justice priority
constructs.description: Importance assigned to substantively just outcomes independent of procedure alone.

constructs.name: Retributive punishment
constructs.description: Support for punishment as deserved response to wrongdoing.

constructs.name: Deterrent punishment
constructs.description: Support for punishment as a means of deterring future wrongdoing.

constructs.name: Rehabilitative / restorative punishment
constructs.description: Support for rehabilitation, repair, restoration, or reintegration as purposes of criminal justice.

constructs.name: Legal positivism / nonpositivism
constructs.description: Whether legal validity is conceptually separable from morality or partly dependent on moral facts.

constructs.name: Cosmopolitan political scope
constructs.description: Degree to which political duties and institutions should extend beyond national boundaries.

constructs.name: National / particular political obligation
constructs.description: Degree to which compatriot or national membership generates special political obligations.

constructs.name: Institutional pluralism / polycentricity
constructs.description: Preference for overlapping, competitive, decentralized, or polycentric institutions rather than unitary authority.

constructs.name: Reform vs rupture orientation
constructs.description: Preference for gradual institutional reform versus discontinuous or revolutionary replacement.

constructs.name: Religious authority in public law
constructs.description: Degree to which religious doctrines or authorities should have independent standing in public law or political rule.

constructs.name: Human-life grounding of moral standards
constructs.description: Whether requirements of human life and flourishing ground objective moral standards. Separate from mere biological description or current preferences.

constructs.name: Choice-to-live conditionality of moral reasons
constructs.description: Whether moral requirements are conditional on choosing to live. This is not identical to making morality relative to any passing desire.

constructs.name: Ethical egoism as a normative principle
constructs.description: The universal moral prescription to prioritize one’s own good; not a claim about actual motives or a permission for personal projects.

constructs.name: Rational egoism about practical reasons
constructs.description: Whether one’s own welfare supplies the ultimate standard of practical rationality; distinct from moral rightness and descriptive motivation.

constructs.name: Ownness and revisable allegiance to ideals
constructs.description: Original operationalization of non-subjection to fixed ideals and revisable appropriation of projects. An interpretive proposal, not a validated Stirner scale.

constructs.name: Promissory self-binding
constructs.description: Whether a voluntary promise itself creates a defeasible reason beyond current desire; not an exceptionless duty or legal remedy rule.

constructs.name: Continuing endorsement and exit from commitments
constructs.description: Whether continued association or service requires renewed endorsement; separate from duties to repair induced reliance and from valid waiver.

constructs.name: Reliance-based reasons for performance or repair
constructs.description: Reasons generated by induced expectations and reliance; separable from promises as normative powers and from specific-performance enforcement.

constructs.name: Elective other-regarding concern
constructs.description: Possibility of voluntarily caring about another as an end without making universal self-sacrifice a duty. Not the intensity of experienced affection.

constructs.name: Fallibilism about knowledge
constructs.description: Whether knowledge can coexist with the possibility of error; distinct from willingness to revise, skepticism, and infallibility of a nonpropositional perceptual process.

constructs.name: Pragmatic clarification through consequences
constructs.description: Clarifying disputed ideas through conceivable differences in experience or conduct; not treating expediency as truth.

constructs.name: Concepts as revisable instruments of inquiry
constructs.description: Conceptual revision and usefulness in inquiry; compatible with constraints from mind-independent reality.

constructs.name: Noninferential foundations of justification
constructs.description: Whether some epistemic warrant is not derived from other beliefs. Foundationalism need not make every foundation infallible.

constructs.name: Contextual certainty
constructs.description: Whether sufficient evidence in a context can warrant certainty despite possible later revision. Not dogmatic immunity to evidence.

constructs.name: Perceptual-conceptual basis of factual warrant
constructs.description: Grounding claims about the concrete external world in sensory evidence integrated by reasoning; not a priori rationalism or rejecting scientific inference.

constructs.name: Abstract-object commitment
constructs.description: Existence of abstract objects such as numbers, distinct from realism about universals and ordinary physical objects.

constructs.name: Universals commitment
constructs.description: Whether numerically the same universal is instantiated by distinct things; separate from shared resemblance and mental concepts.

constructs.name: Ordinary external-world independence
constructs.description: Independence of ordinary concrete objects from thought; does not settle social ontology, universals, or the method of ontology.

constructs.name: Easy or deflationary approach to ontology
constructs.description: Using conceptual application conditions and ordinary empirical inquiry rather than an additional heavyweight existence test. Compatibility with realism remains disputed.

constructs.name: Institutional dependence without elimination
constructs.description: Whether institution-dependent entities can be real; different from independence from all persons or a moral collective duty.

constructs.name: Individual-level explanation of social processes
constructs.description: Whether social explanations must be grounded in agents and their interactions; not normative individualism or denial of aggregate patterns.

constructs.name: Preinstitutional grounding of rights
constructs.description: Whether persons have basic rights independently of social recognition; distinct from the form and strength of a particular property regime.

constructs.name: Institutional and instrumental justification of rights
constructs.description: Justification of rights in terms of agency, cooperation or institutional consequences. May coexist with status-based justification.

constructs.name: Territorial monopoly of final legal force
constructs.description: Whether a single final rights-protecting legal authority is necessary within a territory. Separate from arbitrary command and unqualified obedience.

constructs.name: Nonstate adjudication and protective provision
constructs.description: Institutional possibility and acceptability of nonstate legal services; separate from rejection of general political obligation and from assuming all commons require markets.

constructs.name: Institutional value independent of obedience
constructs.description: Practical justification and participation without conceding a general content-independent moral duty. Not a disguised abolition scale.

constructs.name: Institutional state-abolition preference
constructs.description: Preference for replacing states, independent of rejecting general obligation. This does not measure timing or methods of transition.

constructs.name: Contractual remedies distinct from continuing assent
constructs.description: Justification of compensatory or protective remedies despite withdrawal, distinct from compulsory personal performance or legal advice about existing law.

constructs.name: Psychological egoism
constructs.description: Descriptive universal claim that ultimate motives concern one’s own welfare. Distinguish desire ownership from desire content.

constructs.name: Incompatibilist condition on free agency
constructs.description: Whether causal determinism excludes free agency, distinct from the belief that determinism is true or ordinary freedom from coercion.

constructs.name: Constitutionally protected federal division
constructs.description: A normative preference for entrenched powers at both national and regional levels, with neither level able to withdraw the other’s assigned powers unilaterally. This is narrower than decentralization.

constructs.name: Direct act-consequence criterion
constructs.description: A scoped maximizing act-outcome criterion for moral rightness. This is distinct from generic attention to outcomes, rule consequentialism, and utilitarian welfare theory.

constructs.name: Consequence-justified rule criterion
constructs.description: A scoped rule-based moral rightness criterion. Consequences ultimately justify the rule, and conformity to it can determine an act’s rightness even when that act alone has a better outcome. This is distinct from a useful rule of thumb and an independent duty.

constructs.name: Welfarist outcome value
constructs.description: Whether only the well-being of affected beings ultimately makes an outcome better or worse, distinct from a theory of personal well-being, aggregation, and moral rightness.

constructs.name: Total-well-being maximizing act criterion
constructs.description: Whether the best total-well-being outcome among available actions determines individual-act moral rightness, including in the specified valid-promise conflict. Distinct from generic consequence concern, act-versus-rule criterion, welfare-only outcome value, and a complete ethical theory.

constructs.name: Democratic and worker control over production (scoped preference)
constructs.description: Whether the respondent favors effective worker or democratically accountable public control over production decisions in two stated settings. Distinct from common ownership of selected resources, workplace voting alone, redistribution, market coordination, formal legal title, and a complete economic-system identity.

constructs.name: General happiness as ultimate moral standard
constructs.description: Whether general happiness has final justificatory authority when moral rules, duties, or judgments conflict, without selecting an act-versus-rule implementation.
